findings.claim: LCME retains tri-hybrid persistent memory orchestration with SQLite, vectors and knowledge-graph/FTS retrieval, while Hippocampus neural retrieval is used only when ready and mature; otherwise retrieval falls back to the conventional path.

Current retrieval source explicitly records that immature Neural Cortex weights reduced P@5 from 1.0 to 0.08; the historical redesign commit reports P@5 0.40 to 1.00 after removing 7,213 entity vectors, adding stopword filtering, relevance-dominant scoring and maturity gates.
findings.next_test: Any learned ClayGraph/UnifiedDB retrieval layer must beat a frozen non-neural baseline under cold-start, mature, OOD and restart conditions before it can become authoritative.

findings.claim: LCME ingestion invalidates retrieval caches and deliberately prevents chat-origin turns from flooding the hot fact buffer; retrieval also skips chat-origin records as user memories.
findings.implication: Unified cognitive storage needs explicit source-class semantics; conversational transcript presence must not automatically imply durable factual memory identity.

findings.claim: SOMA implemented an adaptive LoRA lifecycle with interaction scoring, scheduled CPU training, drift/similarity/NaN deploy gates, snapshots, EMA blending, GGUF conversion/hot reload and rollback. The introduction commit reports 104 conversations scored, 80 qualified and a complete 18.7-minute CPU cycle that passed its safety check and deployed an adapter.
findings.constraint: The reported run is repository evidence, not independent replication; final Clay-native training still needs held-out, leakage-resistant validation.

findings.claim: Project Engine v3 implemented persistent goals with metrics/decomposition, an entity-relation world model, hard/soft policy state, tool-outcome learning, five-step action chaining, heartbeat scheduling and checkpoint recovery. Its commit reports a 39-second zero-Claude-token autonomy cycle and a 331-second five-step autonomous chain.
findings.constraint: Historical unrestricted-system-access and credential-handling choices are not inherited; only orchestration/state/recovery mechanisms are candidates.

earned_work_mappings.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: Current ClayGraph/UnifiedDB differential benchmark shows these retrieval/fallback lessons do not transfer or a simpler current baseline dominates them.

branch_feedback.claygraph: Use LCME as a differential baseline family, especially source-class filtering and neural maturity gates; do not assume learned retrieval wins.
